newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ISRAEL, Jan 14 - Haifa - No labour problems. Four vessels discharging at berth (3 general cargo, 1 bulker), 4 containers, 2 tankers. 4 Vessels waiting at anchorage of which 2 general cargo to discharge, 2 tankers, 2 vessels under repair/dry-docked, 3 awaiting orders. 2 Vessels due with 1-2 days delay expected. Ashdod - No labour problems. 15 Vessels berthed and operating of which 9 general cargo discharging, 1 bulker loading, 2 bulkers discharging, 3 container vessels. Vessels waiting at anchorage of which 4 general cargo to discharge, 2 bulkers to load, 1 bulker to discharge, 4 containers. 1-2 Days berthing delay expected. Eilat - Two general cargo vessels loading at berth, 1 container, 1 passenger. 1 Vessel due.

MOZAMBIQUE, Jan 13 - Nacala - Port working normally on a first come-first served basis. No restrictions on berthing and sailing during night time. Draft restrictions, 9.5 metres plus height of tide at general cargo berths and 14 metres at container berths. One tug available. Beira - General cargo berths working normally on a first come-first served basis. Container terminal/other terminals - Working normally. Pilotage now possible 24 hours per day for vessels up to 140 metres loa with a maximum draft of 7.5 metres. Two tugs fully operational. Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangements with the port captain. Maputo - Pilotage now possible 24 hours a day for vessels up to 120 metres loa with a maximum draft of 9 metres. Two tugs (one out of order). Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangement with the port captain. All berths are working normally and expected to remain so (first come-first served basis). Draft restriction in the channel is 9.0 metres less 0.5 metres plus the rise of tide.
NAMIBIA, Jan 13 - Walvis Bay - Port working normally.

NIGERIA, Jan 13 - Lagos - There has been a leak in the Escravos/Lagos gas pipeline and it is reported that Lagos gas power station has lost 70 percent of capacity. Major power black-outs are expected in the Lagos area. As yet, there are no indications as to when repairs to the pipeline will be completed. All crude oil terminals reported as working normally and vessels loading according to programme.

SOUTH AFRICA, Jan 13 - Richards Bay - General cargo berths - Delays of 12-24 hours can be expected from 14/1. Bulk import berths - No delays foreseen for the coming week except for a minor delay on berth 701 between sailing/berthing of two vessels. Bulk export berths (minerals etc.) - Congested at present and berthing delays of up to 48 hours can be expected from 13-20/1. General - No major delays at coal terminal at present. Two vessels expected at inner anchorage from 14/1 for repairs and bunker. Bulk coal berths - At present 2 vessels at outer anchorage, 3 berthed and 18 due up to and including 20/1. Berthing delays of approx. 24 hours can be expected from 18/1.

Durban - Container terminal - No delays at present. Point/New Pier/Maydon wharf berths - Working normally for general cargo vessels. Maize terminal (Maydon wharf 8) - No vessels for January. Bunker supplies - Fluid - Delays of 8 hours in supplying bunkers can be expected due to bunching of vessels. Dry-dock/floating dock - Fully booked for January and February. East London - General cargo/combi terminal berths - Busy but no delays expected at this stage. Dry-dock - Booked from 1471 to 24/1, thereafter open for bookings. COPPER - Moving in small parcels of 2,500 metric tons per month in containers to the Far East. Gas oil pipeline - Under utilised. WHEAT imports - One vessel in port. Tankers - Expect to be busy until the end of January.

Port Elizabeth - Working normally with 3 vessels in port. No delays expected general cargo, ore or tanker berths. Container berth - Under pressure but no delays expected. Cape Town - Breakbulk berths - Working normally with vessels berthing and operating on arrival. Container terminal - No delays expected for the coming week bunker berths. No delays for the coming week. Bunker enquiries have increased since 1/1. Dry-docks and repair quay - Fully occupied at present, with booking essential. Saldanha Bay - Port working normally.

TUNISIA, Jan 11 - Sousse - Four vessels in port of which 3 discharging (1 vegetable oil, 1 general cargo, 1 timber), 1 loading bulk salt. 10 Vessels waiting, no delays. Tunis - Seven vessels in port of which 1 tanker discharging wine, 2 under arrest, 2 discharging wood-pulp, 1 discharging steel coils, 1 general cargo vessel. Rades - Five vessels in port of which 3 ro/ros, 1 discharging grain, 1 loading containers. La Goulette - North side - 1 Passenger vessel, 1 vessel discharging maize, 1 tanker discharging soya beans. South side - 1 Vessel discharging grain, 1 loading clinker. 1 Vessel in roads.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, Jan 5-11 - 182 Vessels of which 76 containers, 11 general cargo, 2 general cargo/containers, 4 bulk carriers, 5 car carriers, 21 tankers, 7 naval vessels, 2 UAE naval vessels, 9 bunkers/under repair/taking stores etc., 7 dhows, 8 barges, 9 tugs, 16 supply boats, 1 passenger vessel, 1 crane barge, 2 refrigerator vessels, 1 ngl tanker, 5 container vessels loading at berth, 24 due. 8 General cargo vessels discharging at berth, 3 under repair/laid-up, 8 due. 3 Tankers discharging at berth, 1 bunkering, 8 under repair/laid-up.

YEMEN, Jan 12 - Hodeidah - All berths occupied, 7 vessels berthed of which 1 bulk wheat, 2 wheat flour, 1 rice, 1 timber, 1 containers, 1 general cargo. 4 Vessels anchored of which 1 sugar, 1 timber, 1 frozen cargo, 1 containers. Berthing delays, general cargo up to 2 days, bagged cargoes up to 4 days, bulk cargo up to 6 days, containers up to 1 day. Mokha - One idle vessel berthed after discharging wheat flour, 1 palm oil vessel waiting at anchorage, no berthing delays.
